questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Limit of a Rational Function with a Radical in the Numerator
questions.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x} & =\frac{\sqrt{0+1}-1}{0}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(\sqrt{x+1}-1)(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{(\sqrt{x+1})}^{2}-{1}^{2}}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x+1-1}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{0+1}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{\sqrt{x+7}-2}{x+3} & =\frac{\sqrt{-3+7}-2}{-3+3}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{\sqrt{x+7}-2}{x+3} & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{(\sqrt{x+7}-2)(\sqrt{x+7}+2)}{(x+3)(\sqrt{x+7}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{(\sqrt{x+7})^{2}-{2}^{2}}{(x+3)(\sqrt{x+7}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{(x+7)-4}{(x+3)(\sqrt{x+7}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{x+3}{(x+3)(\sqrt{x+7}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{\cancel{x+3}}{\cancel{(x+3)}(\sqrt{x+7}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -3}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+7}+2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{-3+7}+2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}+2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2+2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2x-10\sqrt{x}}{x-25} & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2(x-5\sqrt{x})}{x-25} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2(x-5\sqrt{x})(x+5\sqrt{x})}{(x-25)(x+5\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2({x}^{2}-{(5\sqrt{x})}^{2})}{(x-25)(x+5\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2({x}^{2}-25x)}{(x-25)(x+5\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2x(x-25)}{(x-25)(x+5\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {25}^{-}}\frac{2x}{x+5\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{2(25)}{25+5\sqrt{25}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Limit of a Rational Function with a Radical in the Denominator
questions.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=2$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{x-2}{\sqrt{3x+1}-\sqrt{7}} & =\frac{2-2}{\sqrt{3(2)+1}-\sqrt{7}} \\  & =\frac{2-2}{\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{7}} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{x-2}{\sqrt{3x+1}-\sqrt{7}} & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})}{(\sqrt{3x+1}-\sqrt{7})(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})}{(\sqrt{3x+1})^{2}-(\sqrt{7})^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})}{3x+1-7} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})}{3x-6} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(x-2)(\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7})}{3(x-2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{\sqrt{3x+1}+\sqrt{7}}{3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3(2)+1}+\sqrt{7}}{3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}+\sqrt{7}}{3} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{7}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=4$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{3x-3}-3} & =\frac{4-4}{\sqrt{3(4)-3}-3}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{x-4}{\sqrt{3x-3}-3} & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{(x-4)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)}{(\sqrt{3x-3}-3)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{(x-4)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)}{{(\sqrt{3x-3})}^{2}-{3}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{(x-4)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)}{3x-3-9} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{(x-4)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)}{3x-12} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{(x-4)(\sqrt{3x-3}+3)}{3(x-4)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{\sqrt{3x-3}+3}{3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3(4)-3}+3}{3} \\  & =\frac{3+3}{3} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{x-64}{\sqrt{4x}-16} & =\frac{64-64}{\sqrt{4(64)}-16}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{x-64}{\sqrt{4x}-16} & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{(x-64)(\sqrt{4x}+16)}{(\sqrt{4x}-16)(\sqrt{4x}+16)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{(x-64)(\sqrt{4x}+16)}{(\sqrt{4x})^{2}-{16}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{(x-64)(\sqrt{4x}+16)}{4x-256} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{(x-64)(\sqrt{4x}+16)}{4(x-64)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{\cancel{(x-64)}(\sqrt{4x}+16)}{4\cancel{(x-64)}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 64}\frac{\sqrt{4x}+16}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4(64)}+16}{4} \\  & =\frac{16+16}{4} \\  & =\frac{32}{4} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}\frac{x-2\sqrt{x}}{x-4} & =\frac{4-2\sqrt{4}}{4-4}=\frac{0}{0},\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\eqalign{
	\lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {x - 2\sqrt{x}} {x - 4} &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {(x -2 \sqrt{x})(x+2\sqrt x)} {(x - 4)(x+2\sqrt x)} \
            &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {x^2-\left(2\sqrt{x}\right)^2} {(x - 4)(x+2\sqrt x)} \
	    &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {x^2-4x} {(x - 4)(x+2\sqrt x)} \
	    &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {x(x-4)} {(x - 4)(x+2\sqrt x)} \
	    &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {x} {x+2\sqrt x} \
	    &= \lim_{x \to 4^+} \dfrac {4} {4+2\sqrt4} \
	    &=\dfrac 1 2.
	}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=0$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{3x}{\sqrt{x+1}-1} & =\frac{3\cdot 0}{\sqrt{0+1}-1}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\eqalign{
\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac {3x} {\sqrt{x + 1} - 1} 
	&=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{(3x)(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{(\sqrt{x + 1} - 1)(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}\
	&=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{3x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{\left(\sqrt{x+1}\right)^2-1^2}\
	&=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{3x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{x+1-1}\
	&=\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{3x(\sqrt{x+1}+1)}{x}\
	&=\lim_{x\to 0}3(\sqrt{x+1}+1)\
&=3(\sqrt{0+1}+1)\
	&=6.
}
$$
